supplying_copy: NT-1582-M -- the NT half of the 2007 Maximus Scriptorius reprint (S06), photographs of an original 1582 Rheims Fogny copy. The base exemplar NT-1582-B lacks this leaf outright.
LIMITING FACTOR: M's raster is 1-BIT CCITT at ~380 ppi, letter-size re-lay-out, ABBYY-processed, from a 2007 print-on-demand reproduction, and NO continuous-tone original exists to acquire. Letter identity and diacritics are secure at 3-4x. The w/vv discrimination is NOT secure at this ceiling (see w_regime) and CANNOT BE RAISED, because no better image of this leaf exists in any copy -- B lacks it, and X's is a spliced low-resolution substitute. This is a real ceiling, not a pending acquisition.

body.note: Foliate strapwork headpiece band -- interlaced acanthus/palmette on a ruled ground, NO human or animal figures. This is a SETTING DISCRIMINANT: the 1633 setting's Preface headpiece is a foliate GROTESQUE carrying human/animal figures.

copy_specific_marks.kind: manuscript reader's annotations, in the physical copy photographed
observed: underlining beneath 'ent time' and 'ate' (line 31, partial strokes)
two marginal flourish/manicule-like pen strokes in the right margin
copy_specific_marks.why_it_matters: These are pen marks made by a reader of the ORIGINAL copy. A facsimile in the strict sense -- a redrawing -- would not carry them. They are independent physical corroboration that S06's images are PHOTOGRAPHS of an original early-modern copy, which is the claim on which M's admission rests (MASTERPLAN 1.1). They are NOT part of the printed text and are excluded from the transcription.

w_regime.FINDING: THIS FACE MIXES w AND vv, and the w/vv call must therefore be GLYPH-DRIVEN, exactly as long-ſ already is. It cannot be applied as a per-face blanket rule.
w_regime.capital_proof: 'VVhich' (line 21), zoomed 4x: a CAP-HEIGHT V followed by an X-HEIGHT v, two separate sorts with a clear gap and different heights. Not a W sort.
w_regime.single_w_sort: 'word' (line 27), zoomed 4x: a single sort whose medial strokes JOIN at a shared apex serif, with no gap -- a genuine w. It stands on the SAME LINE as 'vve', which is two sorts.
w_regime.vv_instances: vvhy, nevv, vvhole, vvorke, vve, vvhich, vvritte, vvel, alvvaies, vvere, knovven, novv, othervviſe, vvholy, vviſedom, vvritte
w_regime.CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM, and deliberately not raised. At 380 ppi bitonal a w-sort cut vv-style and a true vv pair are near the discrimination limit, and the guidelines warn that over-zooming past ~5x pixelates the sort and proves nothing. All zooms were held at or below 4x.
w_regime.OPEN FOR SIR: The standing per-face table gives 'NT 1582 roman body = real w'. That was settled on the SCRIPTURE body face. This leaf is set in the smaller PRELIMS prose face, which is a different fount -- so this finding does NOT trigger the global flip the guidelines contemplate, and no existing scripture transcription is affected. What it does mean is that a blanket vv->w or w->vv pass over the NT prelims would be WRONG in both directions. Transcribed here as seen.

setting_identification.against_1633: The 1633 setting of this same page, transcribed at ground-truth/matter-nt-preface.json from NT-1582-F, differs in ways no two impressions of one forme can: 'auncient' vs 'ancient', 'maner' vs 'manner', 'text:& of the' vs 'text ; and of the', display heading breaking 'THE PREFACE TO / THE READER TREATING OF' vs 'THE / PREFACE TO / THE READER TREATING', and a strapwork headpiece vs a figured grotesque. Letter-count differences are decisive -- they are resettings, not inking variation.
setting_identification.corroboration: Independently consistent with the blank-margin foxing proof that F's Preface p.1 leaf is natively the 1633 Princeton copy's (MASTERPLAN 1.4).

uncertain.note: Spaces before ':' are preserved where seen ('language : or', 'many : or') and absent where not ('Engliſh: of the', 'text:& of the'). At this raster fine inter-word spacing is MEDIUM confidence; the presence/absence pattern is reported as observed, not regularised.
No space after the comma before '&' as set; medium confidence.
Underlined in manuscript; the printed word is unambiguous.

method: Read from M's own raster (embedded CCITT stencil pulled from S06.pdf via witness/extract_pdf_leaves.py, polarity normalised by minority-class) in 7 overlapping horizontal bands at 0.67x, with targeted 4x crops for the w-regime capital ('VVhich'), the single-w sort ('word') and a vv control ('othervviſe'). Zoom held at or below 4x throughout.
confidence: High on the display heading, the drop-cap paragraph and the roman prose. High on long-ſ (glyph-driven, read per character). MEDIUM on w/vv discrimination and on fine French spacing -- both at M's raster ceiling, which cannot be improved for this leaf. Medium-high on the marginalia, which are set in the smallest face on the page.
